key_insight: ScenA generates realistic multi-speaker audio scenes by conditioning a text-to-audio foundation model on multiple reference voices and in-the-wild priors, rather than relying on rigid speaker tags or clean speech-only pipelines. This lets the model produce conversational audio with ambient texture, not just separated vocal turns.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between structured multi-speaker dialogue systems and real-world conversations. Existing methods often need per-turn labels, multi-stream transcripts, or speaker embeddings, and they tend to miss background ambience and natural interaction cues.
method: Condition a pretrained text-to-audio flow-matching foundation model directly on multiple reference voice samples.
Use in-the-wild audio priors so the model learns realistic conversational texture and ambient context.
Generate full multi-speaker audio scenes without requiring explicit speaker diarization-style supervision for each turn.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this points to a simpler way to synthesize realistic dialogue data with stronger environmental realism. It can improve research and applications in audio generation, simulation, dataset augmentation, and multimodal agent training.
